intro: Before you stands Gök Medrese, a madrasa and hospital in Sivas province, built in 1271. It is named for the turquoise tiles that sheathe its minarets, and its portal carries vegetal carving and a zodiac of twelve animals found nowhere else.
history: This madrasa was built at Sivas in 1271 for the vizier Sahip Ata, and it takes its name from the turquoise tiles sheathing its minarets. The vegetal carving of its portal and its zodiac of twelve animals form a sequence with no equal in Anatolia. And it was not alone: three great madrasas went up in Sivas in that same year.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the twin tiled minarets and the portal. Look closely at the zodiac reliefs, and then step through to the courtyard iwans.
facts: Did you know? Three madrasas going up at once in 1271 shows that Sivas was being deliberately turned into a centre of learning under Ilkhanid rule. This one takes its name from the turquoise tiles on its minarets, and the zodiac of twelve animals on its portal is without equal in Anatolia.
outro: This brings our tour of Gök Medrese to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Enjoy your visit.
